name: host_hardening

sysctl_config.rationale: The safeguard writes Linux kernel hardening settings.

journald_config.rationale: The safeguard writes the Linux journald rate-limit drop-in.

storage.rationale: Linux-only system configuration is verified by the safeguard file check.

description: Make kernel hangs and oopses produce diagnostics: enable sysrq, set hung-task/softlockup/NMI panic, and rate-limit journald so UFW BLOCK floods don't drown panic info

linux.reason: Host safeguards mutate host state and cannot ship in a desktop bundle.

macos.reason: Host safeguards mutate host state and cannot ship in a desktop bundle.

windows.reason: Host safeguards mutate host state and cannot ship in a desktop bundle.

oops_policy.description: What a kernel oops should do. panic-and-dump turns an oops into a panic so kdump captures a vmcore; it requires an armed crash kernel and costs a full outage for any single-task kernel fault. log-and-continue records the oops and keeps the host up, which suits a workstation that is also an operator's daily driver.

softlockup_policy.description: What a CPU soft lockup should do. warn records the stall and lets a host that recovers keep running. panic reboots on any stall of 20 seconds or more, which on a heavily loaded host is a self-inflicted outage rather than a diagnostic.

hung_task_timeout_secs.description: Seconds a task may stay blocked in D state before the kernel logs it. 0 disables the detector.

linux.evidence: Manifest-declared applicability; no host-sampled qualification recorded.

macos.evidence: A mechanism exists but no implementation is wired for this host OS.

windows.evidence: A mechanism exists but no implementation is wired for this host OS.
